harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the cluster: node1 as writable primary, node2 and node3 as read-only physical standbys using pg_basebackup, replication slots, and a SCRAM-authenticated replicator role. Verified writes on node1 propagate to both standbys and that standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of PostgreSQL, replication streaming, and data.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql/postgresql-contrib (v16) on node1, node2, node3
Created 'replicator' replication role with generated password on node1
Configured node1 postgresql.conf: listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Added pg_hba.conf entries on node1 allowing scram-sha-256 replication connections from node2/node3 IPs
Created physical replication slots node2_slot and node3_slot on node1
Wiped node2/node3 data directories and ran pg_basebackup (-R) from node1 to bootstrap standbys with standby.signal and primary_conninfo
Set listen_addresses on node2/node3 and started PostgreSQL as standbys
Verified pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming, and confirmed insert on primary appears on both standbys plus standby write-rejection
Captured pre-restart boot_id on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling until reachable
Verified changed boot_id on each node post-restart
Verified PostgreSQL active and correct recovery state on each node after its restart (standbys recovery=t with prior data intact; primary recovery=f and accepted new write)
Confirmed post-primary-restart write replicated to both standbys, proving replication survives full-cluster restart

evidence.summary: apt install output and dpkg -l confirm postgresql-16 installed on node1, node2, node3

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as primary (wal_level, listen_addresses, replication role, pg_hba)
evidence.summary: Replicator role created; postgresql.conf shows wal_level=replica, listen_addresses='*'; pg_hba.conf has replication entries for node2/node3; restarted and confirmed active with wal_level=replica

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 provisioned as standbys via base backup from primary
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup completed 100% on both nodes; postgresql.auto.conf shows primary_conninfo pointing at node1 and standby.signal present

evidence.requirement: Standbys are read-only and streaming from primary
evidence.summary: pg_is_in_recovery() returns true on node2/node3; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both nodes in 'streaming' state

evidence.requirement: Changes on primary visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 (repl_test id=1) is visible via SELECT on both node2 and node3; INSERT attempts on standbys fail with read-only transaction error

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id c96a02ae...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 189d9e44...; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=false, accepted new write; pg_stat_replication shows both standbys reconnected and streaming

evidence.requirement: node2 (standby) restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 1e0cb179...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 56806364...; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=true, prior data (id=1) intact, later saw post-primary-restart row (id=2) replicated

evidence.requirement: node3 (standby) restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 29011044...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to ee96a72f...; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=true, prior data intact, later saw post-primary-restart row (id=2) replicated

evidence.requirement: Full-cluster restart does not break replication or data
evidence.summary: After all three nodes were restarted, a new write on node1 (id=2 'post-restart primary write') was confirmed present on both node2 and node3, proving end-to-end replication survived the full sequence
